title: Scleromalacia Perforans: The Silent Necrosis
summary: Scleromalacia perforans represents the most severe, non-inflammatory manifestation of ocular rheumatoid arthritis. This board-certified deep dive covers its devastating pathophysiology, systemic associations, and surgical management strategies.

sections.title: 1. Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Scleromalacia perforans is a rare, severe, painless form of scleritis characterized by necrotizing scleral thinning without overt inflammation. It is pathognomonic for long-standing, seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). The underlying mechanism involves occlusive vasculitis of the episcleral/scleral vessels leading to tissue infarction and sequestration.

sections.title: 3. Clinical Features & Exam Findings
content: Painless "sequestration" of scleral tissue.
Absence of injection (white eye).
Visible underlying uveal tissue (dark brown/blue).
Intact overlying conjunctiva until rupture.
Thinning progressing to actual staphyloma formation.

sections.title: 4. Red Flags: Impending Rupture
content: Increase in size of the necrotic plaque.
Development of a localized staphyloma.
A sudden drop in intraocular pressure (IOP) suggesting occult leak.
New onset of pain (indicates transition to active inflammatory scleritis).
Presence of overlying conjunctival epithelial defect.

content.explanation: S: Systemic Control (DMARDs/Biologics), T: Tissue Support (Grafts), A: Avoid Steroid Drops (can worsen melt), B: Biologics (Rituximab/Infliximab).

sections.title: 6. Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Serology (RF, Anti-CCP, ANA, ANCA, ESR/CRP).
Step 2: Slit-lamp exam with scleral transillumination.
Step 3: B-scan Ultrasound to assess posterior staphyloma size.
Step 4: OCT (Anterior Segment) to measure exact scleral thickness.
Step 5: Rheumatology consult for immediate systemic escalation.

sections.title: 7. Surgical Intervention Steps
content: 1. Debridement: Remove necrotic tissue (if loose/sequestrated).
2. Patch Grafting: Use scleral patch graft (donor sclera or pericardium).
3. Tectonic Support: Suture graft using 8-0 or 9-0 Vicryl/Nylon.
4. Conjunctival Flap: Cover the area with a vascularized conjunctival pedicle flap to promote healing.
5. Tissue Glue: Use Histoacryl (Cyanoacrylate) only for micro-perforations.

rows: Blue sclera is diffuse, not patchy

sections.title: 9. Key Clinical Pearls
content: NEVER perform cataract surgery in an eye with active scleromalacia; wait for systemic stability.
Topical corticosteroids are generally CONTRAINDICATED as they inhibit collagen synthesis and exacerbate scleral melting.
The risk of globe perforation is highest during minor eye rubbing or sudden IOP spikes.
Rituximab (anti-CD20) is currently the gold-standard systemic therapy for refractory RA-associated scleromalacia.
